test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following is correct regarding Gitam?

I. It is the simplest type of composition.

II. It is very simple in construction, with an easy and melodious flow of music.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the realm of **Indian Classical Music**, specifically the **Carnatic** tradition, **Gitam** (also spelled **Geetham**) is recognized as the **simplest type of musical composition**. It is designed primarily for students who have moved past basic exercises to understand the melodic structure of a **Raga**. *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• A **Gitam** is characterized by its **very simple construction**. Unlike more complex forms like **Kritis** or **Varnas**, it does not have distinct sections like **Pallavi**, **Anupallavi**, and **Charana**. Instead, it features a **continuous and melodious flow** of music. *Hence, statement II is correct.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both I and II.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structural Features of Gitam:**

 
 
• The term **Gitam** literally translates to "**song**." In these compositions, the **Sahitya** (lyrics) and the **Svara** (notes) are given equal importance. There are no **Sangatis** (variations) or complex **Gamaka** (ornamentations) used, making it easy for beginners to perform.
 
• It is typically set to **Madhyama Kala** (medium tempo). The **Sahitya** often consists of praises for **Gods** and **Goddesses**, reflecting the **Bhakti** (devotional) essence of **Indian music**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• **Purandara Dasa**, widely revered as the **Pitamaha** (grandfather) of **Carnatic music**, is credited with standardizing the teaching methodology, which includes the **Pillari Gitams**.
 
• The **Pillari Gitams** are usually the first few songs taught to students and are composed in praise of **Lord Ganesha**, such as the famous "**Sri Gananatha**" in **Raga Malahari**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Gitams:**
 
 
• **Samanya Gitam**: Also known as **Sanchari Gitam**, these are ordinary compositions where the **Sahitya** is religious or philosophical.
 
• **Lakshana Gitam**: These are unique because the **Sahitya** describes the **Lakshanas** (characteristics) of the **Raga** itself, including its **Arohana** (ascending scale), **Avarohana** (descending scale), and **Varjya** notes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Musical Components:**

 
 
• **Tala**: Gitams are usually set to simple **Suladi Sapta Talas** like **Rupaka**, **Triputa**, **Dhruva**, and **Matya**.
 
• **Language**: The lyrics are commonly found in **Sanskrit**, **Kannada**, or a specialized musical dialect known as **Bhandira Bhasha**.
 
• **Pedagogical Role**: Learning **Gitams** is a crucial milestone for a student to grasp the **Svarupa** (personality) of different **Ragas** like **Kalyani**, **Sankarabharanam**, or **Mohanam** before advancing to the **Varnam** stage.
